subject: PII scoping and transfer safeguards — NeuroHealth integration
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@neurohealth.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Victor Chen <victor.chen@neurohealth.ai>, security@neurohealth.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifications on PII scope and transfers for Redwood integration

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the low-latency routing. Before we move ahead with the pilot, our security questionnaire flagged a few items we need to clarify around PII handling and international transfers: 

1) Can you confirm which fields in request payloads are persistently logged and for how long? We need retention windows for identifiers (email, name, patient_id).
2) Which Redwood subprocessors will touch identifiable tokens or logs for the hosted integration? Please include any cloud providers and observability vendors.
3) If data is routed to a non-US region (failover/DR), what controls are in place for cross-border transfer?

Would appreciate a short write-up and any diagrams you can share. We attached a redline of the questionnaire where we annotated these rows — happy to route to legal if you prefer.

Best,
Elena Morris
Head of Security Operations
NeuroHealth

Attachments: NeuroHealth_SSQ_annotated.pdf (annotated questionnaire)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <elena@neurohealth.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on PII scope and transfers for Redwood integration

Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Adding a concise summary below and attaching a simple dataflow and access matrix. I also looped in Rishi (legal) and Hannah (privacy/infrastructure) for any contractual or KMS details.

Quick answers: 
- Persistent logging: Redwood does not persist raw request bodies for hosted API calls by default. We retain structured telemetry (latency, token counts, model used) for 90 days. Identifiers in logs are redacted at ingestion; any customer-requested retention or logging of full payloads requires explicit opt-in and is surfaced in the contract (DPA annex).
- Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor roster. For hosted customers the primary subprocessors that may see non-redacted identifiers (only with explicit opt-in) are our cloud infra provider (CloudNorth), managed logging provider (LogForge), and our backup storage vendor (SafeArchive). For dedicated/private deployments, we can restrict that list per the deployment contract.
- Cross-border failover: We route by policy and include automatic encryption-in-transit (TLS1.3) and server-side encryption-at-rest. For transfers we rely on SCCs for EU customers and documented transfer impact assessments for other jurisdictions. For NeuroHealth specifically, we can restrict processing to US regions only for the pilot and enable a VPC private deployment if you require no egress to third-party clouds.

Attachments: dataflow-neurohealth-v1.pdf (diagram), access-matrix-neurohealth.xlsx (role-level access)

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether you need the pilot constrained to US-only processing.
2) If NeuroHealth requires KMS key custody, let us know and we’ll scope a Bring-Your-Own-Key option.

- Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security (Integrations)
Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <elena@neurohealth.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on PII scope and transfers for Redwood integration

Elena — quick follow-up from infra privacy perspective: 

- KMS custody: if NeuroHealth wants customer-managed keys we offer KMS integration (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private. For hosted trials we can enable a key-wrapping workflow where your key is used to envelope storage keys; however, long-term BYOK requires Dedicated or Private deployment.
- Access controls: internal access to keys/logs is restricted via role-based access in our IAM; access to decrypted payloads requires a documented justification and is audited. The access matrix attached shows teams and typical approval paths.

If NeuroHealth legal wants wording for the DPA annex (KMS, retention, subprocessor list), Rishi can draft suggested language.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morris <elena@neurohealth.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on PII scope and transfers for Redwood integration

Elena — thanks for the detailed questions. I drafted suggested DPA annex language addressing: retention windows (90d default telemetry, 0d default request body), subprocessor disclosure, and a clause for regional processing restriction and BYOK requirements. Attaching the draft clause below and copying a DocuSign link for a short pilot addendum if you want to sign off quickly.

--- DPA annex (excerpt):
1) Data Processing Scope: Redwood will process request payloads on behalf of NeuroHealth. By default, Redwood does not persist raw request bodies. Any retention of identifiers or full payloads will be set by mutual agreement in the DPA annex.
2) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and notify NeuroHealth 30 days prior to adding a subprocessor that may access unredacted identifiers.
3) Cross-border Transfers: Redwood will process data in the regions specified in the order. Transfers outside specified regions require documented transfer impact assessment and appropriate transfer mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy or other lawful basis).
4) KMS & Key Custody: Customer-managed keys are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers may use an envelope key arrangement upon request.

DocuSign pilot addendum: https://www.docusign.com/pilot-addendum/neurohealth

If that looks good I can share the full annex with tracked changes.

— Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
